newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European bourses retreat but dollar surges.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European bourses retreat but dollar surges.

text.p: Leading European stock markets retreated from record highs on Friday as Wall Street got off to an uncertain start, but there was no holding the dollar back.

Shares in London and Frankfurt stormed higher in the morning, buoyed by Wall Street's record close on Thursday, a dollar at 30-months highs and -- for British investors -- relief when an interest rate hike failed to materialise.
The Paris bourse also headed into record territory, although with less conviction than its European counterparts.

But prices slipped as passions cooled, backed by Wall Street's hesitant opening. Major markets remained above Thursday's record closes but London was particularly jaded, with the FTSE index only just holding above the 4,200 point level which was breached for the first time in early trade.

Wall Street was mixed in early trade, with a weak bond market inhibiting a follow through from yesterday's late rally. The Dow Jones Industrial did start climbing and by mid morning it was up 36.56 points at 6,801.93.
But that did nothing to inspire London, where the FTSE was well off its early 4,218 high, up a paltry 5.3 at 4202.3.

Dealers blamed the expiry of FTSE index options for the early leap, which was also fuelled by relief that finance minister Kenneth Clarke had decided against raising interest rates following relatively benign inflation data.
"We have seen good buying around," said Andrew Bell, head of investment trust research at BZW "though an artificial element today has been the options expiry".
German dealers were unexcited by an early surge in the DAX index through the 3,000 point barrier for the first time.
They had spoken excitedly of bottles of champagne hidden away for the market hitting such a level.
Once the DAX reached the magic marker, however, caution took over. "Of course we are happy to see the 3,000 mark but it doesn't mean the start of anything big," said one dealer.
The DAX closed at 3,001.37, up 8.06 points.

French shares likewise hit an all time high before losing some of the gains. Again the reasons were the dollar and Wall Street plus special factors such as the sale by luxury goods manufacturer LVMH of a stake in British group Guinness Plc.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 12.40 points at 2,420.17 after hitting a historic high at 2,426.13.
But the dollar was unreservedly bullish. It powered to a near 31-month high against the mark after U.S. trade data gave it the ammunition to breach stiff resistance levels.
"It was the smaller than expected U.S. trade deficit data that gave the dollar a boost," said Craig Shute, fixed income analyst at Bear Stearns.
The market had spent the morning wrestling with tough technical resistance at 1.6050-60 marks.

Then came the data showing the trade deficit for November was $8.40 billion, widening from $8.01 billion in the previous month. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast on average a deficit of 9.8 billion dollars for November.
The dollar sailed through technical barriers to the day's high of 1.6125 marks after the trade figures, up from 1.5957 at the European close on Thursday.
At 1530 GMT it was at 1.6100 marks and 117.15 yen, compared with 1.5958 and 116.52 in late European trade on Thursday.
Analysts said figures pointing to a robust U.S. economy were likely to give the dollar another boost.

"That (stronger than expected data) would add to speculation of a Fed tightening, and that on the whole is cautiously positive for the dollar, so long as there's a belief that the actual tightening won't be overly aggressive," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief European economist at BankAmerica.
Industrial production data for December, also released on Friday, were also robust. It rose 0.8 percent from the previous month, above expectations for a 0.6 percent rise.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 117 yen and 1.6100 marks, compared with 116.53 and 1.5945 late on Thursday.
Sterling firmed to 2.6895 marks from 2.6745 late on Thursday. The French franc eased to 3.3732 marks from 3.3748.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1545 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was 7.2 points higher at 4,204.7, the first time it has gone through 4,200.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index broke through 3,000 before closing up 8.06 at 3,001.37 points.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 16.79 at 2,424.26, also above Thursday's record close of 2,407.77.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $354.85, up from Thursday's close of $353.35. Silver was slightly stronger at $4.77, up four cents from the previous London close.
